who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), executor of plan 5 T3/T4, int-1112
what: An idle hello-world daemon held 4,912 MB of footprint, 1,131 MB of it an unattributed 'allocator kept' remainder: freed mimalloc pages of threads that never collected (expansion threads waiting on a channel were never woken for a give-back), fiber stacks and parked workers' stack pages nobody advised away, and a names reader keeping 64 generations, each name its own Arc<str>. heaps.rs's doc also said mimalloc's committed count never falls on a purge, which is false (mi_arena_purge decommits).
cost: a gigabyte held idle with no row naming it, read as 'allocator overhead'
cause: a give-back reached only threads that registered as a pool worker, and nothing counted stacks, so pages held by a thread outside the pool or below a parked stack had no owner that would let them go
class: memory held by a thread that no give-back reaches and no counter names
prevention: every thread that allocates counts in the give-back handshake (count_heap_settles) and is woken through heap_wakes_by; stacks are counted (stack bytes) and given back below the frame as a worker parks; the threads row names how many threads hold heaps
fix: expansion threads settle as they go idle and are woken for a give-back; parked pool workers exit their idle fibers and advise their stack below the frame away (MADV_DONTNEED / MADV_FREE_REUSABLE); the names reader keeps WINDOW + 1 generations in one buffer each; stack bytes, threads and idle-over rows; a modelled raise is held to one work thread's share. Controls: a give-back with the wake off stays Pending; 3 of 4 makers settling stays committed; the stack test without the advice keeps its pages; RetainSixtyFour exceeds the bound; the whole-budget forecast starts one node, not two. Not built or run yet.
